description: We are ERDEM NOVA, an innovative team from Erdem College in Gaziantep, Türkiye, led by an Information Technology Teacher. We focus on artificial intelligence, prompt engineering, STEM, software development, and space exploration. Our mission is to develop creative solutions using NASA's open data. We welcome passionate team members interested in Python, AI, data analysis, astronomy, engineering, and digital design. Together, we aim to turn bold ideas into real-world solutions.
summary:
SpaceTwin is an interactive, data-driven web application developed by Team Erdem NOVA for NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026. It addresses the challenge of identifying Earth locations that can help researchers and students explore environmental conditions relevant to future Moon and Mars habitats.

Unlike a purely visual simulation, SpaceTwin connects to NASA's POWER API to retrieve authentic monthly temperature and precipitation data for selected Earth locations. Users can explore established analog environments and candidate sites in Türkiye, examine 12-month climate charts, and compare environmental characteristics.

The platform combines geographic exploration, transparent data sources, and educational interpretation in an accessible web interface. It uses historical NASA scientific datasets retrieved through live API requests, not real-time satellite measurements.

SpaceTwin supports evidence-based exploration while clearly distinguishing preliminary candidates from scientifically validated planetary analogs.
details:
Project Overview

SpaceTwin is a web-based educational research prototype developed to investigate Earth environments that may provide useful analog conditions for future Moon and Mars exploration.

How It Works

Users select an Earth location from an interactive schematic map. The application sends a location-based request to NASA's POWER Monthly Point API and retrieves historical environmental data.

The platform processes monthly near-surface air temperature (T2M) and precipitation (PRECTOTCORR), displays 12-month visualizations, and calculates annual indicators using day-weighted monthly values.

Locations and Research Scope

SpaceTwin explores established terrestrial analog environments, including the Atacama Desert, Haughton Crater, and Death Valley, alongside exploratory locations in Türkiye such as Cappadocia, Karapınar, Nemrut Caldera, and the Lake Salda region.

These locations are presented for environmental investigation and educational comparison. Their inclusion does not establish scientifically validated equivalence to Moon or Mars environments.

Technologies and NASA Resources

The application uses web technologies, JavaScript-based data processing, interactive visualizations, and the NASA POWER API.

NASA POWER provides scientific environmental datasets derived from atmospheric data products and modeling systems, including reanalysis products that assimilate observations.

SpaceTwin retrieves published historical datasets through live API requests. It does not claim to receive instantaneous measurements directly from satellites.

Innovation and Educational Value

The project's central contribution is connecting an accessible planetary analog exploration interface with verifiable NASA environmental data.

Rather than presenting fabricated simulation values, SpaceTwin allows users to examine actual NASA datasets and understand the scientific limitations of environmental comparisons.

Limitations and Future Development

The current map is schematic, and the project does not calculate a scientifically validated planetary similarity score.

Future research may incorporate NASA GPM/IMERG precipitation observations, SMAP soil moisture products, and planetary topographic datasets from MOLA and LOLA, subject to successful integration and verification.

Project Access

Live application: https://erdemnova-spacetwin.netlify.app/

Source code and documentation: https://github.com/vahitkoray/ErdemNOVA-SpaceTwin
